user.title: Hey Auri Client
user.description: Configure the thin Home Assistant frontend to call the hosted SaaS backend.

error.invalid_guest_phone_number: Enter a valid US/Canada phone number (for example, +16045551234 or 6045551234).
error.memory_settings_missing: Enter the database host, name and username to turn memory on.
error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the PostgreSQL server with these settings, or the database doesn't exist.
error.invalid_auth: The database rejected the username or password.
error.psycopg2_missing: The PostgreSQL driver (psycopg2) isn't installed in this Home Assistant. Home Assistant OS and Container include it; on a Core install run pip install psycopg2-binary in its virtual environment.
error.pgvector_missing: This PostgreSQL server doesn't have the pgvector extension. On Home Assistant OS use the TimescaleDB app (add-on), which includes it; with Docker use the pgvector/pgvector:pg17 image.
error.insufficient_privilege: This database user can't enable pgvector or create the auri_memory and auri_guest_memory schemas. Have an administrator run CREATE EXTENSION vector; in this database and grant the user CREATE on it.
error.vault_public: That folder is inside www, which Home Assistant serves without a login. Choose a folder outside it, such as /share/MyVault.
error.vault_not_allowed: Home Assistant isn't allowed to write there. Add the folder to allowlist_external_dirs in configuration.yaml.
error.vault_not_writable: Home Assistant can't write to that folder.
error.guest_memory_needs_memory: Set up Memory first: guest memory uses the same database.

init.title: Hey Auri Client options
init.description: Choose which settings group to edit.

guest.title: Guest settings
guest.description: Configure booking and guest-facing instruction defaults.

data_description.guest_phone_number: Only US/Canada numbers are supported. Use +1 format (for example, +16045551234) or a 10-digit local number (for example, 6045551234).
data_description.property_knowledge: Where non-IoT items are and how to use them. Example: Extra towels are in the hallway linen closet on the second shelf. Used towels should be placed in the laundry basket in the bathroom before checkout.
data_description.local_recommendations: What is around the house. Example: For coffee, the host recommends Corner Bean Cafe on West 4th Avenue. It is a cozy local coffee shop that is good for morning coffee, pastries, and a quick breakfast before heading out. It is usually quieter before 9 AM.
data_description.guest_memory_enabled: In guest mode, Auri remembers what guests tell it and learns from their conversations each night, for this stay only. It's kept apart from your own memory, in your PostgreSQL database (Memory must be set up). Erased an hour after check-out (then closed until the next booking), and started again for each new booking ID (or new check-in when there's no booking ID).
data_description.reset_guest_memory: Erase all guest memory now and start again from the guest name, guest count, check-in and check-out, and notes above.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Let Auri remember facts, preferences and past conversations in owner mode, stored in your own PostgreSQL database (with the pgvector extension). Each night the day's conversation is sent to Auri's backend to be summarized; it isn't kept there. Saving tests the connection without changing anything.

data.memory_vault_include_private: Include private memories in the vault copy

data_description.memory_db_host: For the TimescaleDB app on Home Assistant OS: 77b2833f-timescaledb.
data_description.memory_db_password: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
data_description.memory_vault_path: Auri keeps a readable copy here (Auri/Daily notes and Auri/Memory.md), for example /share/MyVault. Edits made in the vault aren't read back.
data_description.memory_day_boundary_hour: Conversation before this hour counts toward the previous day. Each day is processed about 15 minutes after it ends.
data_description.memory_share_household: Auri uses everyone's memories, private ones too, whoever is speaking, including an unknown speaker on a voice satellite. Anyone near a satellite could hear them, visitors too.

logins.title: Who uses each login
logins.description: When someone uses Assist signed in to Home Assistant, Auri uses the memories of the person their login is linked to. Choose someone else if another person uses a login (for example, you sign in as admin). Choose Shared for a login the household shares, like a wall tablet: Auri then treats the speaker as unknown, as on a voice satellite. Choose Not a person for a login a service uses, like Zigbee2MQTT's MQTT login: its person isn't counted as a household member. Nothing changes in Home Assistant.
